# To connect to your data you will need to go through these steps:

## Manual Steps:

1. Connect to a VPN, so that you appear to be 'within the university library'. You do this by hand, usually using the FortiClient app. See tech support pages (https://information-services.ed.ac.uk/computing/desktop-personal/vpn) on how to set it up (if you haven't already)

## R code steps:

2. Connect to your secure 'online harddrive' (called DataStore) using `connectDatastore(...)`, see examples. Below code will create a 'virtual connection' to your DataStore harddrive. By default, this is set to be named R: so please check that you don't have an R: drive before starting.
3. You can peek into the DataStore folder with `openDatastoreFolder()` - it will appear as if it was a new harddrive or folder on your computer. Do not copy files from there by hand. Use R to load that data instead.
4. Now you can use the DataStore files. Load and save the data using provided functions like `loadCsvWithDatastore(your_filename)` or `saveCsvWithDatastore(your_filename, some_data)`. Advanced: There are various helper functions, but if you need to build your own, e.g. you use unusual data format, just use `fileLocationOnDatastore(your_filename)` instead of `your_filename` to get the file's location for saving and loading. So e.g. instead of `load_csv("patients.tsv")` use `load_csv( fileLocationOnDatastore("patients.tsv"))`
5. When done with accessing data, you can disconnect from DataStore with `disconnectDatastore()`

# How to use this is your dissertation

To use this in your dissertation code, bring the file `dataStoreScripts.R` into your project and start your markdown with this like (just once) `source("dataStoreScripts.R")`. It will give you access to all datastore functions demonstrated below. 

```{r}
source("dataStoreScripts.R")
```

# TESTING and EXAMPLES

```{r}
#load testing variables

yourUsername <- "porzecho"
yourDatastoreSpace <- "s1234567" #usually same as username

  if (operatingSystemIsWindows()) {
    # Windows
      yourOrganisationsFolder <- "cmvm.datastore.ed.ac.uk\\cmvm\\cmvm\\groups\\mvm-pgt" 
  } else {
    # Mac
    yourOrganisationsFolder <- "cmvm.datastore.ed.ac.uk/cmvm/cmvm/groups/mvm-pgt"
  }
```

```{r}
# attempt connecting to datastore. If this does not work for you. 1. check VPN 2. Your setup might require typing in the password, in which case refer to the `terminal_commands` file

connectDatastore(yourUsername, yourDatastoreSpace, yourOrganisationsFolder, disconnectFirst = FALSE)
```



```{r}
openDatastoreFolder()
```

```{r}
# save random file
test_data <- data.frame(name=c("a","b","c"), age=c(10,20,33))
saveCsvWithDatastore(test_data, "test123.csv")
```

```{r}
# load random file
loadCsvWithDatastore("test123.csv")
```

```{r}
disconnectDatastore()
```
